title: Wave model and wave phenomena
summary: Transverse and longitudinal waves, v = fλ, sound and the electromagnetic spectrum; reflection, refraction and Snell’s law, total internal reflection, diffraction, double-slit interference and (HL) single-slit diffraction and gratings.

keyterms.definition: A wave whose oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer, e.g. light.
A wave whose oscillations are parallel to the direction of energy transfer, e.g. sound.
Distance between two adjacent points in phase on a wave, e.g. crest to crest.
Speed of energy transfer by the wave: v = fλ.
The family of transverse EM waves, all travelling at c in vacuum, from radio to gamma.
n = c/v; Snell’s law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.
Angle of incidence giving a 90° refraction angle: sin θ_c = n₂/n₁, for light going into a less dense medium.
Spreading of waves through a gap or around an obstacle; most noticeable when the gap ≈ λ.
When waves overlap, the resultant displacement is the vector sum of the individual displacements.
Difference in distance from two sources; nλ gives constructive, (n + ½)λ destructive interference for in-phase sources.
Sources with the same frequency and a constant phase difference.
Many equally spaced slits giving sharp bright maxima at nλ = d sin θ.

lessons.title: Wave properties and the EM spectrum

questions.prompt: Which type of wave is sound in air?
questions.explanation: Air particles oscillate parallel to the direction of travel, producing compressions and rarefactions.

questions.text: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 4.0 m. Its speed is ___ m s⁻¹.

questions.explanation: Polarization restricts oscillations to one plane perpendicular to travel, which is possible only for transverse waves.

questions.prompt: A radio station broadcasts at 100 MHz. What is the wavelength? (c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)
Order these EM waves from longest to shortest wavelength.
questions.explanation: Wavelength decreases and frequency (and photon energy) increases along the spectrum.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Region of high pressure in a sound wave
Maximum positive displacement of a transverse wave

questions.explanation: These terms describe features of wave motion.

questions.prompt: When a wave passes from deep to shallow water, its speed decreases. Which quantity stays the same?
questions.explanation: Frequency is set by the source; since v = fλ, the wavelength decreases with the speed.

questions.statement: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum.
questions.explanation: All EM waves travel at c ≈ 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ in vacuum.

questions.text: On a displacement–distance graph, the distance between adjacent crests is the ___.
questions.explanation: A displacement–distance graph shows λ; a displacement–time graph shows the period T.

questions.prompt: Which wave intensity relation is correct for a point source radiating uniformly?
questions.explanation: Power spreads over a sphere of area 4πr², so I = P/4πr². Also I ∝ amplitude².

questions.prompt: Light passes from air into glass (n = 1.50) at 30° incidence. What is the angle of refraction?
questions.explanation: sin θ₂ = sin 30°/1.50 = 0.333, so θ₂ ≈ 19.5°: light bends towards the normal.

questions.text: The critical angle for glass of refractive index 1.50 (into air) is about ___°.

questions.statement: Total internal reflection can occur when light travels from air into water.
questions.explanation: It requires light travelling into a medium with a lower refractive index, e.g. water to air.

questions.prompt: A water wave passes through a gap. Diffraction is most noticeable when
options: the gap is much wider than the wavelength
the gap is about the same size as the wavelength
the wave has a large amplitude
questions.explanation: Significant spreading happens when the aperture is comparable to λ.

questions.prompt: Two coherent sources in phase produce waves that meet at a point with a path difference of 1.5λ. The result is
questions.explanation: A path difference of (n + ½)λ gives antiphase arrival and destructive interference.

questions.text: In a double-slit experiment λ = 600 nm, slit separation d = 0.30 mm and screen distance D = 2.0 m. The fringe spacing is ___ mm.

questions.prompt: Match each wave phenomenon to its description.

pairs.right: Change in direction due to speed change

questions.explanation: These four phenomena are behaviour shared by all waves.

questions.statement: Two separate light bulbs do not produce a visible interference pattern because they are not coherent.
questions.explanation: Their phase relationship changes randomly and rapidly, so fringes wash out.

questions.prompt: In the double-slit experiment, what happens to the fringe spacing if the slits are moved closer together?
questions.explanation: s = λD/d, so a smaller d gives wider fringes.

questions.prompt: Order how an optical fibre transmits a signal.
items: Light enters the core at one end
It strikes the core–cladding boundary above the critical angle
It repeats this along the fibre to the far end
questions.explanation: The cladding has a lower refractive index than the core, allowing total internal reflection.

questions.text: Light of wavelength 500 nm passes through a slit 0.10 mm wide. The angle to the first minimum is ___ × 10⁻³ rad.

questions.prompt: In a single-slit diffraction pattern, the central maximum is
options: the same width as the others
twice as wide as the other maxima
half the width of the others
questions.explanation: The central maximum spans from −λ/b to +λ/b, twice the angular width of the subsidiary maxima.

questions.statement: Making a single slit narrower makes the diffraction pattern spread out more.
questions.explanation: θ = λ/b: smaller b gives a larger angle to the first minimum.

questions.prompt: A grating has 500 lines per mm and is lit with 600 nm light. What is the angle of the first-order maximum?

questions.text: For the grating above (d = 2.0 µm, λ = 600 nm), the highest observable order is n = ___.
questions.explanation: n ≤ d/λ = 3.33, so the highest whole order is 3.

questions.prompt: Compared with a double slit, a diffraction grating produces maxima that are
options: closer together for the same d
questions.explanation: Many slits make the constructive condition very precise, giving narrow, bright maxima, ideal for spectroscopy.

questions.statement: In a real double-slit pattern, the intensity of the fringes is modulated by the single-slit diffraction envelope.
questions.explanation: Each slit has finite width, so the two-slit fringes sit inside a single-slit envelope.

questions.prompt: Match each formula to its situation.
questions.explanation: Each formula describes a different diffraction or interference arrangement.

questions.prompt: White light passes through a grating. In each first-order spectrum, which colour is deviated most?
questions.explanation: sin θ = λ/d, so the longest wavelength (red) is diffracted through the largest angle.

questions.prompt: Reflection of light from a medium of higher refractive index causes a phase change of
questions.explanation: Reflection at a boundary with a denser medium introduces a phase shift of π, important in thin-film interference.
